name: Partner Portal feasibility analysis
description:
h1. Why?

The Partner Portal PRD (Tier 1 for 2026) defines the full intended scope of a unified space for all Shoptet partner types. Before any delivery scope can be committed, we need to know what is technically feasible, at what cost, and in what order.

The PRD flags feasibility as its top risk: _"Integration with existing CRM and Salesforce — risk of delays and technical obstacles. Mitigation: verify feasibility ASAP."_ Two more red risks (data quality in migration, DevRel team capacity) and four red open questions (OQ-04, OQ-18, OQ-19, OQ-20) cannot be closed without this analysis. OQ-20 (WordPress: retain or replace) explicitly blocks the overall architecture.

Today the partner data and processes are fragmented across Salesforce, internal CRM, 3 WordPress instances (CZ/SK/HU) and SharePoint, with much of the administration handled manually over email. Partners and add-ons account for at least 14% of company profit and 1.3M MRR (September 2025), and ~20% of API team capacity goes to partner support.

h1. What?

One analysis child issue per key feature area from the PRD, plus one cross-cutting integration & architecture analysis. Each child answers the same questions for its area:

- Which existing systems hold the data (Salesforce, internal CRM/CMS, WordPress, Keboola) and which of them must be read from vs. written to?
- Is the needed integration/API available today, does it need extending, or is it missing entirely?
- Rough effort size (T-shirt) and the main technical unknowns.
- Blockers and dependencies on other feature areas or on other teams.
- Recommendation: MVP candidate / later phase / out of scope.

Deliberately _not_ in scope of this epic: UX/design work, final delivery estimates, sprint planning, and any implementation. This is a decision input, not a commitment.

h1. Acceptance criteria

Every child analysis issue is completed with the five questions above answered

Cross-cutting integration analysis states who owns master data for portal ↔ CRM ↔ Salesforce (OQ-19)

WordPress retain-vs-replace recommendation is documented (OQ-20)

Data migration scope from 3 WP instances is assessed (OQ-04)

Each feature area has a T-shirt size and an MVP / later / out-of-scope recommendation

Consolidated summary is reviewed with DevRel, API, Addons and Partnership teams

Result feeds the MVP scope decision for 2026 planning
